title: Norse at L'Anse aux Meadows
description: Tree rings show Norse settlers cutting wood at this site in 1021, the only confirmed Norse settlement in North America.

title: Cabot's landfall
description: John Cabot, sailing for Henry VII of England, reaches the coast of North America and reports seas full of cod.

title: Cartier claims the land for France
description: Jacques Cartier raises a cross at Gaspé on the first of three voyages that explore the St Lawrence.

title: Quebec founded
description: Samuel de Champlain builds a trading post that becomes the capital of New France.

title: Montreal founded
description: A mission settlement named Ville-Marie is founded on the island of Montreal.

title: Hudson's Bay Company chartered
description: Charles II grants a company of London merchants the trade of all lands draining into Hudson Bay, about a third of modern Canada.

title: Great Peace of Montreal
description: New France and about forty First Nations, including the Iroquois, end nearly a century of war.

title: Expulsion of the Acadians
description: British authorities begin deporting the French-speaking Acadians, more than ten thousand of whom are removed.

title: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
description: A British army under Wolfe defeats Montcalm outside Quebec, both generals dying, and French rule in Canada ends the next year.

title: Treaty of Paris
description: At the end of the Seven Years' War France cedes Canada and all its claims east of the Mississippi to Britain.

title: Quebec Act
description: The British Parliament guarantees the Catholic religion and French civil law in Quebec.

title: Loyalists arrive
description: Tens of thousands of refugees from the American Revolution settle in the British colonies, giving them an English-speaking population.

title: Upper and Lower Canada created
description: The Constitutional Act divides Quebec into two provinces, each with an elected assembly.

title: Mackenzie reaches the Pacific
description: Alexander Mackenzie completes the first recorded crossing of North America north of Mexico.

title: Battle of Queenston Heights
description: British, Canadian and Mohawk forces throw back an American invasion, though General Isaac Brock is killed.

title: Rebellions of 1837
description: Risings in Lower and then Upper Canada against government by appointed councils are put down, and lead Britain to rethink how the colonies are ruled.

title: Province of Canada formed
description: The Act of Union joins Upper and Lower Canada under one legislature.

title: Responsible government
description: The governor accepts a ministry answerable to the elected assembly, first in Nova Scotia and then in Canada under Baldwin and LaFontaine.

title: Charlottetown Conference
description: Delegates from the colonies meet and agree in principle to a federal union.

title: Confederation
description: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick are joined as the Dominion of Canada.

title: Red River Rebellion
description: The Métis under Louis Riel resist the transfer of the North-West to Canada and win the creation of the province of Manitoba.

title: Indian Act
description: Parliament passes the law that governs First Nations status, reserves and band government, and that remains in force in amended form.

title: Last spike of the Canadian Pacific
description: The railway to the Pacific promised to British Columbia is completed, tying the country together.

title: Louis Riel hanged
description: The leader of the North-West Rebellion is executed for treason, embittering relations between French and English Canada.

title: Klondike gold found
description: A strike on a tributary of the Klondike sets off a rush of about 100,000 people to the Yukon.

title: Battle of Vimy Ridge
description: The four divisions of the Canadian Corps, fighting together for the first time, take the ridge.

title: Halifax Explosion
description: A munitions ship explodes in the harbour after a collision, killing about 2,000 people.

title: Persons Case
description: The Privy Council rules that women are persons who may sit in the Senate.

title: Statute of Westminster
description: The British Parliament gives up the power to legislate for the dominions, making Canada independent in law.

title: Newfoundland joins Canada
description: After two referendums Newfoundland becomes the tenth province.

title: Quiet Revolution begins
description: The election of Jean Lesage's Liberals begins a decade in which Quebec takes schools and hospitals from the church and its nationalism grows.

title: Maple Leaf flag
description: Canada raises its own flag in place of the Red Ensign.

title: October Crisis
description: After the Front de libération du Québec kidnaps a British diplomat and a provincial minister, the government invokes the War Measures Act.

title: Constitution patriated
description: The Queen proclaims the Constitution Act, with its Charter of Rights and Freedoms, ending Britain's role in amending Canada's constitution.

title: Quebec referendum
description: Quebec votes against sovereignty by 50.6 to 49.4 percent.

title: Nunavut created
description: The eastern Arctic becomes a territory with an Inuit majority.

title: Apology for residential schools
description: The prime minister apologises in Parliament for the schools that took about 150,000 Indigenous children from their families.
